original_question: Which gene is an ABC transporter, and whose mutations are associated with a pigmentation disorder?

final_qi.question: Which gene is an ABC transporter, and whose mutations are associated with a pigmentation disorder?
final_qi.long_answer: ABCB6 encodes ATP-binding cassette sub-family B member 6, an ABC transporter present in mitochondria and melanosomes. Heterozygous loss-of-function mutations in ABCB6 have been shown to cause dyschromatosis universalis hereditaria, a disorder marked by mottled hyper- and hypopigmented skin lesions, firmly linking this ABC transporter gene to a pigmentation disorder.

0.question: Which ABC transporter gene is associated with a pigmentation disorder?

final_answer.long_answer: ABCB6 encodes an ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporter. Pathogenic variants in this gene disrupt melanosome function and melanin handling, and have been unequivocally shown to cause the pigmentary genodermatosis dyschromatosis universalis hereditaria, linking an ABC transporter to a pigmentation disorder.
